Parent session downloads upstream tqdm, spawns helpers, patches API and metadata, fixes contrib concurrent behavior, adds nested aliases, verifies, and closes.

inspect_pyproject child examines package metadata, copies and patches overlapping files, verifies imports and tests, and returns packaging guidance.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a complete tqdm project implementation with upstream-compatible package modules, public exports, packaging metadata, local tests, optional integrations, and prompt-specific import compatibility.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned final implementation and integration while spawning helpers for export/API inspection, pyproject/package metadata, and submit-harness discovery.
parallel.implementation: Copied upstream tqdm 4.70.0, patched root exports and optional metadata, fixed contrib.concurrent behavior, and later added a nested tqdm/tqdm compatibility package for nonstandard prompt imports.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All actors wrote into the same /workspace. One child re-extracted the upstream tree after parent patches, but the parent and children later repatched, verified, and delivered the final workspace.
parallel.verification: Ran import probes, focused pytest files, full pytest twice, pandas-specific tests after installing pandas, and captured that no submit command was available; official evaluation then passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final evaluator-visible task failure remained. The unresolved process issue was recovered rework from shared-workspace overwrite and inability to run a submit tool inside the agent environment.

serial.requirements: Recognized the need for an installable upstream-compatible tqdm project with broadened exports, version fallback, contrib aliases, support files, and verification.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned all exploration, source copy, implementation, packaging, verification, and final response without delegated subtasks or shared-workspace concurrency.
serial.implementation: Copied upstream tqdm 4.70.0 and patched top-level API exports, contrib product/logging aliases, version fallback, pyproject extras, and support files such as tox and asv config.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial workspace was populated once through a temporary sdist copy and then patched in place by the same actor, so there was no cross-agent merge or provenance conflict.
serial.verification: Ran import-level checks, full bundled pytest with 156 passed and 4 skipped, and built a wheel with pip wheel; it also confirmed no submit command existed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final artifact did not include or verify the nested tqdm/tqdm compatibility package, and the official completed evaluation failed despite local pytest and wheel success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel pursued a complete upstream-compatible tqdm project and also noticed the prompt-specific nonstandard tqdm.tqdm.* import requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial pursued upstream-compatible tqdm plus exports and metadata, but its recorded work did not cover nested tqdm.tqdm.* compatibility.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The requirement coverage difference is the nested compatibility layer: parallel added and verified it; serial stopped at normal top-level and contrib exports.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed auxiliary investigation into export, pyproject, and submit helpers while the parent retained final implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all responsibilities in one execution thread and therefore had one owner for source copy, patching, verification, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Delegation gave parallel extra exploratory coverage but introduced shared-workspace coordination risk; serial avoided that risk but also lacked a separate prompt-import check.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent had enough prompt/interface context to create a compatibility package and then adjusted alias internals after import failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial validated normal package imports and star-import surfaces but did not create or verify a nested alias namespace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The interface difference is concrete: parallel implemented the prompt-facing import alias contract; serial's checks focused on regular tqdm, contrib, and top-level names.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied upstream, patched exports and metadata, replaced contrib.concurrent logic to avoid a deadlock, and added tqdm/tqdm/__init__.py aliases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied upstream and patched top-level exports, contrib aliases, version fallback, pyproject extras, and support files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's implementation had the hidden-compatible nested alias layer and an extra concurrent-helper correction; serial omitted the nested layer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved at least some child results, interrupted long-running helpers, and continued parent-owned implementation through verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the single agent moved directly from local checks to final response after tests and wheel build.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had coordination overhead and recovered from child interruptions, but the useful differentiator was parent follow-through, not a missing join; serial had no result-handoff surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents wrote into the same /workspace; after the parent patched final-tree files, a child broadly extracted the upstream tree into that workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial populated the workspace once from a temporary source extraction and then patched it with the same actor, so no cross-agent overwrite occurred.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a real shared-state overwrite/rework episode, while serial's single-writer path avoided merge collisions; this adverse episode was recovered and did not explain the pass/fail split.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reran targeted imports, contrib concurrent checks, pandas tests, full pytest with 164 passed and 3 skipped, and then official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran imports, full pytest with 156 passed and 4 skipped, built a wheel, and then official evaluation failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had strong local verification, but parallel added verification around the compatibility layer and broader optional coverage; serial's local suite did not expose the missing nested alias requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more time and tool activity due to children and rework but closed within budget, with no host timeout and official pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial was shorter, also no host timeout, and closed after local pytest/wheel success despite the official hidden failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel paid coordination overhead but used it to reach a more complete final artifact; serial conserved budget but closed before finding the nested import gap.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is parallel_only_pass. Parallel passed because it added and debugged a prompt-specific nested compatibility package for nonstandard tqdm.tqdm.* import paths after normal upstream/export work. Serial failed despite local pytest and wheel success because it delivered only the upstream-style package plus top-level/contrib exports and never added or tested the nested compatibility namespace.
parallel_contributors: Parent added tqdm/tqdm/__init__.py for nonstandard tqdm.tqdm.* imports and then fixed import-cycle and optional-dependency alias problems.
Parent reran full pytest after the compatibility layer and optional pandas coverage, leaving no local verification gap that the official evaluator exposed.
serial_contributors: Serial patched normal top-level exports, contrib aliases, metadata, and version behavior, but its recorded final artifact did not include nested tqdm/tqdm compatibility.
Serial verification covered bundled pytest and wheel build but did not exercise the prompt-facing tqdm.tqdm.* namespace.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial omission of the nested compatibility package is an ordinary coverage and implementation miss, not a retained parallel coordination error.
Parallel's contrib.concurrent fix and broader optional test pass improved robustness, but the strongest evidenced discordant requirement is nested import compatibility.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
